quote: A hundred and seventy Campanians, headed by the Blosii who were brothers, had formed a conspiracy to set fire to all these at one hour of the night
notes: Campanian plot to burn the Roman soldiers' huts at Capua was betrayed by a slave and suppressed by summary execution (livy:en:27:3).

quote: The consul refusing to submit to the people what lay in his own power, and forbidding the praetor to do so, the plebeian tribunes put the question
notes: Consul Laevinus clashed with senate and tribunes over who should be dictator for the elections, fled to Sicily, and Marcellus then named Quintus Fulvius dictator as the commons ordered (livy:en:27:5).

quote: it was hardly constitutional that a chief magistrate should be continued in office
notes: Tribunes threatened to block the election because dictator Fulvius was presiding over his own candidacy, until both sides agreed to abide by the senate's decision and Fulvius was elected (livy:en:27:6).

quote: the patricians denying that Caius Mamilius Vitulus, who was a plebeian candidate, ought to be allowed to stand
notes: Patricians contested a plebeian candidacy for chief curio, the matter passed from tribunes to senate to people, and Mamilius became the first plebeian chief curio (livy:en:27:8).

quote: On entering the senate, Lucius Licinius, the praetor, led him out; on which the flamen appealed to the tribunes of the people
notes: The flamen of Jupiter reclaimed the lapsed ancient privilege of a senate seat through tribunician adjudication, restoring the priesthood's political standing (livy:en:27:8).

quote: Twelve of these, for they all had embassies at Rome, told the consuls that they had not whence to furnish either men or money
notes: Twelve of the thirty Latin colonies refused to supply soldiers or money after ten years of levies, and within Book 27 the senate answered only with a tacit reproof while honoring the eighteen loyal colonies (anchor livy:en:27:9, continued 27:10).

quote: the vicesimary gold, which was preserved in the most sacred part of the treasury as a resource in cases of extreme exigency, should be drawn out
notes: Facing the colonies' default, the senate authorized drawing the sacrosanct vicesimary gold reserve from the treasury as an emergency war fund (livy:en:27:10).

quote: The choosing of the senate was delayed by a dispute which arose between the censors about the selection of a chief of the senate
notes: The new censors quarreled over naming the princeps senatus until Cornelius yielded and Fabius was chosen, after which eight senators were expelled and the Cannae equites degraded (livy:en:27:11).

quote: not only the bill for depriving him of his command was thrown out, but the following day he was created consul
notes: Tribune Bibulus's bill to strip Marcellus of his command, debated in the Flaminian circus after his harangues begun in livy:en:27:20, collapsed before Marcellus's self-defense and he was elected consul the next day (anchor livy:en:27:21).

quote: It was asserted that Servilius was not qualified to be plebeian tribune or aedile
notes: Servilius's eligibility for plebeian office was challenged on the ground that his father was alive in enemy hands, but no resolution is recorded in this chapter (livy:en:27:21).

quote: to propose to the people a law to the effect, that a vow should be made to perform these games on a stated day for ever
notes: In response to a pestilence, a law was carried fixing the Apollinarian games on a permanent annual date, converting an ad hoc vow into a standing institution (livy:en:27:23).

quote: seven of the principal senators, with their children, escaped before night, and before the guards were posted at the gates
notes: Fearing Arretium's defection first flagged in livy:en:27:21, Rome garrisoned the town and exacted 120 hostages from senators' children, seven leading senators fleeing before the guards were set (anchor livy:en:27:24).

quote: that the town should be guarded by a garrison, and that all the Tarentines should be kept within their walls
notes: The senate hotly debated punishing the recaptured Tarentines, with Fabius defending them, and deferred final judgment while imposing a garrison (livy:en:27:25).

quote: The case of Marcus Livius, prefect of the citadel of Tarentum, was also debated with no less warmth
notes: The senate split between censuring and rewarding the prefect whose negligence lost Tarentum but who held its citadel, finally remitting his case to the censors amid Fabius's barb that recovery would have been needless had it not been lost (livy:en:27:25).

quote: Titus Quinctius Crispinus, the consul, after having nominated Titus Manlius Torquatus dictator for the purpose of holding the election and celebrating the games, died of his wound
notes: With both consuls dead after the ambush, the dying Crispinus named Manlius Torquatus dictator to hold the elections and games, leaving the commonwealth in a manner orphan (livy:en:27:33).

quote: having withheld their pity from him when arrayed in a mourning garment and a criminal, they now forced upon him the white gown against his will
notes: Marcus Livius, long embittered and withdrawn after his condemnation by the people, was pressed over his own protests into the consulship beside his enemy Nero, the senate later brokering their reconciliation at Fabius's instance in livy:en:27:35 (anchor livy:en:27:34).

quote: The pontiffs also decreed, that thrice nine virgins should go through the city singing a hymn
notes: After the Frusino androgyne and the lightning stroke on Juno Regina's temple, the pontiffs instituted novel expiatory rites including a hymn by the poet Livius and a matrons' offering funded from their dowries (livy:en:27:37).

quote: After each people had stated their grounds of exemption, the exemption of none was allowed, as the enemy was in Italy, except those of Antium and Ostia
notes: The coastal settlers' claim of sacrosanct exemption from the levy was heard and overruled by the senate for all but Antium and Ostia, whose men were bound by oath to stay near home (livy:en:27:38).
